commands.name: add-cookie
commands.description: Adds a single cookie to the current Selenium instance.
commands.notes: Not yet implemented in v2.0.0A1, this message serves as a compatibility guide.

commands.name: add-header
commands.description: Adds an HTTP Header for the current request.

commands.name: add-headers
commands.description: Adds multiple HTTP Headers for the current request via a JSON Object.

commands.name: browser
commands.description: Specifies the browser type. This MUST be the first valid line of the file. If not supplied, defaults to a Firefox instance and user agent.

commands.name: click
commands.description: Clicks the specified button element. Supports ID, NAME, TAG NAME, and XPATH selectors.

commands.name: click-at-position
commands.description: Clicks at a specific point on screen.

commands.name: click-exp
commands.description: Alternative to click; use this if click is causing issues. Supports CSS SELECTOR.

commands.name: close-current-tab
commands.description: Closes the current tab and will close the browser if there's only one open tab.

commands.name: end-javascript
commands.description: Instructs the parser that the end of a JavaScript code block was reached. An error will be thrown if end-javascript is not found within the file (when a start-javascript is present).

commands.name: fill-text
commands.description: Assigns the specified value to the selected element.

commands.name: fill-text-exp
commands.description: More advanced version of fill-text.

commands.name: get-text
commands.description: Gets the text for a specified element. Supports ID, NAME, TAG NAME, and XPATH selectors.

commands.name: open-new-tab
commands.description: A new browser tab is opened, the system will then pause for the number of seconds specified, then visits the requested url.

commands.name: save-as-html
commands.description: Saves the current page's HTML to a file with the specified name.

commands.name: save-as-html-exp
commands.description: Saves the current page's HTML to a file with the specified name but uses different logic; use this if save-as-html doesn't fit your needs.

commands.name: select-element
commands.description: Selects the element associated with the provided selector (if found). This currently works but, there's no logic to access the selected element; this should only be done if you're manually editing the compiled Python script.

commands.name: select-option
commands.description: Selects an <option> from a <select> dropdown menu. Currently only supports <select><option></option></select>.

commands.name: set-custom-useragent
commands.description: Sets a custom user agent at the current point in the script, unlike bamm --set-custom-useragent, which sets this value at startup.

commands.name: start-javascript
commands.description: Instructs the parser to read all following lines as a .js code block, until end-javascript is found; Will throw an error if end-javascript is not found within the file.

commands.name: take-screenshot
commands.description: Takes a screenshot of the browser after executing the previous line. It's recommended to add a "wait-for-seconds" command before executing this.

commands.name: visit
commands.description: Visits a specified URL.

commands.name: wait-for-seconds
commands.description: Waits for the specified number of seconds before continuing. Supports decimals.

commands.name: add-extension
commands.description: Instucts BAMM to download/install a specific extension for the current session.

commands.name: async
commands.description: This indicates to the compiler you want to create an asynchronous script. This should not be done unless you have experience using async functions in Python.

commands.name: bypass-cloudflare
commands.description: Instructs BAMM to compile the current script using anti-fingerprinting techniques to bypass a cloudflare turnstile.
commands.notes: Removed in A4; planned for reintroduction in future rewrite

commands.name: disable-pycache
commands.description: Instructs BAMM to skip generation of the __pycache__ directory and its associated .pyc files.

commands.name: disable-ssl
commands.description: Instructs BAMM to compile the current skip without SSL certificate pinning. Note this is not recommended unless you know what you're doing.
commands.notes: Renamed from no-ssl in A4; both names accepted in A4–A7

commands.name: no-ssl
commands.description: Instructs BAMM to compile the current skip without SSL certificate pinning. Note this is not recommended unless you know what you're doing.
commands.notes: Renamed to disable-ssl in A4; both names accepted in A4–A7

commands.name: run-headless
commands.description: Instructs the compiler to allow headless execution for the duration of the current script.

commands.name: use-http-proxy
commands.description: Uses the entered HTTP proxy for the session. Use "NULL:NULL@IP:PORT" if no user:pass authentication is required.

commands.name: use-https-proxy
commands.description: Uses the entered HTTPS proxy for the session. Use "NULL:NULL@IP:PORT" if no user:pass authentication is required.

commands.name: use-mobile-user-agent
commands.description: Instructs the compiler to return a mobile user agent for the current browser.
commands.notes: Only in A4+ desktop table; instructs compiler to return mobile UA when browser is safari

commands.name: use-socks4-proxy
commands.description: Uses the entered SOCKS4 proxy for the session. Use "NULL:NULL@IP:PORT" if no user:pass authentication is required.

commands.name: use-socks5-proxy
commands.description: Uses the entered SOCKS5 proxy for the session. Use "NULL:NULL@IP:PORT" if no user:pass authentication is required.

commands.name: --allow-multiple-instances
commands.description: Disables the single instance guard, allowing BAMM to run alongside another instance. Intended for automated/headless invocation.

commands.name: --bs
commands.description: Instructs BAMM to use BrowserStack to run the compiled scripts, works on all platforms except ChromeOS, as chromebooks are too underpowered to run selenium.

commands.name: --editbsconf
commands.description: Edit and Overwrite Browserstack's YAML Config via an interactive process. (For advanced users)

commands.name: --exit-on-ext-fail
commands.description: Instructs BAMM to exit with a non-zero exit code when an extension fails to install, instead of warning and continuing. Useful for automated invocation, where a failed extension should fail the run.

commands.name: --force-error
commands.description: Forces a verbose error message, which is helpful for making a bug report.

commands.name: --gui
commands.description: Starts the Graphical User Interface for BAMM.

commands.name: --nohwc
commands.description: Instructs BAMM not to check your system's hardware for compatibility, this should not be done unless you've already verified BAMM can run on your machine.

commands.name: --platform-debug
commands.description: Displays information on the operating system and machine currently running BAMM.

commands.name: --query-display
commands.description: Displays the status of the $DISPLAY variable, use this to check if your system supports BAMM's GUI.

commands.name: --set-custom-useragent
commands.description: Sets the user agent that the browser uses on start up.

commands.name: --version
commands.description: Displays the current version of BAMM, and whether there's a new version available.

commands.name: -n
commands.description: Alias to the new command. Creates a new .bamc file in the userScripts directory, then prompts the user to select a custom text editor to open it. If a custom text editor is not found, the OS default is used.

commands.name: -o
commands.description: Alias to the open command. Opens a .bamc file that exists in the userScripts directory, creating it if it does not, then prompts the user to select a custom text editor to open it. If a custom text editor is not found, the OS default is used.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Adds a .bamc file to the userScripts directory.

commands.name: backup
commands.description: Backs up all application files to BAMM-Backup.zip.

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Deletes the specified application directory, supports 'config', 'userScripts', and 'compiled' as arguments.

commands.name: compile
commands.description: Compiles a .bamc file that isn't located in the userScripts directory

commands.name: delete
commands.description: Deletes the specified .bamc file.

commands.name: help
commands.description: Displays information about the specified command.

commands.name: new
commands.description: Creates a new .BAMC file in the userScripts directory. Prompts the user to select a custom text editor to open the specified file. If a custom text editor is not found, the OS default is used.

commands.name: open
commands.description: Opens a .BAMC file that exists in the userScripts directory. If this file does not exist, the file is automatically created. The user is then prompted to select a custom text editor to open the specified file. If a custom text editor is not found, the OS default is used.

commands.name: restore
commands.description: Looks for a backup of BAMM's data, if the data is found, a restoration is attempted.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Runs the BAMC script provided.

commands.name: uninstall
commands.description: Uninstalls BAMM from the current system.

commands.name: validate
commands.description: Validates the provided BAMC script.
